chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Udhayfir, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If you fear being noticed (in the prayer), it suffices you to place your hand on the ground and not lie down, and he gestured with the tips of his fingers from his right palm, placing it on the ground slightly.' And Abu Ja'far narrated that.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam Muhammad al-Baqir or Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, contextually referring to the other Imam narrating the same ruling)
key_terms.التُّكْأَة: Prostration or pressing down with the forehead/hands; specifically the act of prostrating
key_terms.الشُّهْرَة: Being noticed or becoming known/famous; here referring to fear of attention during worship

ai.seo_question: What is the permissible way to perform a subtle prostration in prayer if one fears being noticed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the fiqh of *khufya* (hidden prayer) for those fearing public scrutiny, offering a pragmatic concession to perform a subtle, semi-prostration by resting the hand lightly on the ground. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility in ritual posture (*sujdah*) to preserve the integrity of prayer when social pressures or modesty concerns arise, distinguishing it from the full, visible prostration required in private.
